title: The Blackroom Collective's Digital Dilemma

scenario.title: The Blackroom Collective's Digital Dilemma
scenario.setting: Tucked in the basement of a 1920s repurposed church in a small Rust Belt town, the Blackroom Collective has resisted full digital photography adoption for 30 straight years. Its walls are lined with scuffed film tanks, frayed red safelight wires, and dog-eared notebooks of member-submitted developing notes. No digital cameras or screens are permitted within its locked front doors, only film, darkroom chemicals, and shared, quiet focus on analog craft.

characters.name: Mara
characters.tendencies: They steward the collective’s budget, track chemical inventory, and enforce shared darkroom rules to keep the space functional for all members.

characters.name: Javi
characters.tendencies: They serve as the collective’s official historian, leading casual tours and sharing stories of the darkroom’s founding to pass along its legacy to new members.

characters.name: Lila
characters.tendencies: They act as the collective’s primary equipment operator, trains new apprentices, and quietly struggles with the urge to explore digital photography on the side.

turns.name: Mara
turns.text:
"Hey folks, quick heads-up—we’re down to half a bottle of stop bath, so swing by the front shelf to grab a labeled voucher if you need it for your print run this week. Please don’t prop your exposed film sheets over the drying rack hook, either; they’re blocking the locked chemical storage bin and create a sharp tripping hazard."
[kneels to restack stray packs of glossy photo paper by the drying station and wipes down the communal film-developing tray with a diluted cleaner]

turns.name: Javi
turns.text:
Welcome to the Blackroom, folks. This basement was repurposed from the church’s old boiler room back in ’78, when our founding members pooled their last few dollars to fix the leaking pipes and haul in a beat-up secondhand enlarger. Most of the original church’s stained glass fragments we found tucked under the floorboards now line the edges of our processing trays.
[I kneel down to pull a tattered leather photo album from under the metal processing sink, flipping open its cover to display a blurry, grainy shot of five grinning teens clustered around a scuffed darkroom enlarger.]

turns.name: Lila
turns.text:
This beat-up enlarger’s been glitching since last spring’s basement flood, so grab the multimeter from the tool bin by the furnace so we can fix the bulb socket before the beginner’s workshop tonight. I’ve been tinkering with a thrift-store digital point-and-shoot on my off hours, too—wanna sneak a test shot of the church’s stained-glass side window after we wrap up?
[I tuck the crumpled color calibration chart I’d been holding under my arm, then reach for the frayed canvas tool bag slung over the workbench leg, my camera strap peeking out from over my shoulder.]

turns.name: Mara
turns.text:
I grabbed the spare multimeter from the furnace-side tool bin earlier while restocking fixer, so you won’t have to dig for it yourself. Just remember to log your use of a stop bath voucher on the whiteboard once you’re done, so we keep accurate inventory counts.
[Hands the compact multimeter over to Lila before straightening to restack a toppled box of photo paper sleeves]

turns.name: Javi
turns.text:
Welcome back, everyone—glad so many of you braved the basement chill for our work night. Shoutout to Mara for flagging the low stop bath supply, and I know Lila’s got her sights set on fixing that finicky enlarger once we’ve got a minute. This space started as a ragtag group turning this old church boiler room into a darkroom back in 1978, and little fixes like this are exactly how we’ve kept that legacy going.
[Gestures first to the front shelf holding the stop bath vouchers, then taps the dented tool bin by the furnace where the multimeter rests.]

turns.name: Lila
turns.text: I already grabbed the multimeter from the furnace-side tool bin—its plastic handle’s cracked, so go easy when you prod the enlarger’s socket. If any new apprentices want a quick walkthrough of basic enlarger troubleshooting after we fix this, I’ve got some cheat sheets stashed in my apron pocket. [twisting the stuck focus knob of the beat-up enlarger just enough to free its gears a little]

dm_opening: DM opening: the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Mara holds the line; the next session's hook waits at the door.
